generalizedRange: Temperate forests of the Russian Far East and northeast China
hook: The world’s rarest big cat wears a winter coat.

story.text: Not many people ever see an Amur leopard. It is a cat of deep forest and far distances, awake mostly at night.
It lives and hunts alone in the vast temperate forests of the Russian Far East and northeast China.
Winter is written into its body. In the coldest months, the hairs of its black-ringed coat grow up to seven centimetres long, and its long furred tail wraps around it for warmth.
For decades it was hunted mercilessly, while logging, forest fires, road building and farming broke its homeland into fragments.
It remains one of the rarest and most endangered leopard subspecies in the world.
And yet the recent story bends toward hope: research shows conservation work is having an effect, and wild numbers are believed to be rising in Russia and China.
To witness the Amur leopard is to hold both truths at once—how close the edge came, and how much a protected forest can still return.
